findings.old_behavior: When --maxmem was specified with a non-zero value N, xmllintMaxmem was incorrectly set to 0 instead of N. Since the custom memory allocators check xmlMemUsed() + size > xmllintMaxmem, a value of 0 caused every allocation to immediately exceed the limit, making --maxmem effectively unusable (instant OOM on first allocation).
findings.new_behavior: xmllintMaxmem is initialized to 0 before the if block. When --maxmem is specified with a non-zero value N, xmllintMaxmem is correctly set to N. The custom memory allocators now enforce the intended memory limit, and --maxmem works as documented.
findings.compatibility_reason: The --maxmem CLI option behavior has changed from broken (always OOM immediately) to working correctly. Any user who previously specified --maxmem would have experienced immediate OOM errors; after the fix, the option actually limits memory usage to the specified value. Users who never used --maxmem are unaffected. This is a bug fix restoring documented behavior.
findings.why_not_internal_only: xmllintMain is the CLI entry point for the xmllint binary. The --maxmem option is a documented CLI interface. Changes to its behavior are externally visible to all users of the xmllint command.
findings.uncertainty: The old behavior was clearly broken (instant OOM), so the fix restores intended documented behavior. Low uncertainty that this is a bug fix. Medium confidence as compatibility change because behavior changed.
findings.recommended_review: Verify that --maxmem now correctly enforces the memory limit by testing with various positive integer values and confirming that OOM triggers at the expected threshold.
findings.test_recommendation: Test --maxmem with values 1, 100, 1000000, and 0 (unlimited/default). Verify that processing succeeds when memory stays under limit and fails with OOM when exceeded. Also verify that not passing --maxmem works as before (no custom allocators installed).
